findings.reason: the plan should route §2's read through the owner it already named, or say why the owner cannot serve raw IDS to `imas_ink.extract.extract_geometry`, instead of hand-rolling a parallel reader.
findings.text: §2's geometry script is to load the jt-60sa catalogue, call `description_store_root_path()`, open the store with `NetCDFTransformEngine.open` and read `wall`/`pf_active`/`magnetics` with `imas.DBEntry`; `imas_ambix/data/description_reader.py:1-6` states it "is the sole machine-description acquisition route" so "consumers do not need to know which source arrays or store layout supplied the description", and its `read_geometry_table` (line 113) plus `transform_machine_description` already resolve format, root and layout from the same catalogue — the plan neither cites nor opens this module. The plan itself already knew this path exists: its own comment at `docs/plans/jt60sa-geometry-and-signal-figures.html:214` says "the reader moves onto artifact_geometry in §1b", yet §1b never moves it and §2 ignores `artifact_geometry` entirely.

findings.reason: two readers of one store drift from each other, and the existing readers already carry the DDv3/DDv4 fallbacks and unresolved-turn guards §2 would have to re-derive.
findings.text: the §2 reader duplicates a route the codebase already owns, and the census of the same reader type is `imas_ambix/gs/artifact_geometry.py:672` (`read_artifact_limiter`, wall→contour), `:302` (`read_artifact_pf_active`, pf_active→filaments/drives) and `:577` (`read_artifact_magnetics`, magnetics→probes/flux loops), all reading the same three IDSs §2 proposes to open; the honest change is to extend this owner, not to fork a second reader beside it.

findings.reason: the plan must either extend the engine view to carry the cached time base (it already carries units) or restate the real distinction — the raw EDDB `UNIT_ATTR` unit and raw sign versus the engine's canonical `target_unit` — before committing to a second read path.
findings.text: §3 adds `read_channel` to `imas_ambix/data/eddb.py` as a cache-specific raw reader placed beside the engine path, justified by the claim that "the engine path those maps feed (`ZarrTransformEngine`, `VirtualZarrView`) returns values with no time base and no unit"; `VirtualArray.attrs` at `imas_ambix/data/virtual_zarr.py:62-71` already returns `"units": rule.target_unit` (with `cocos`, `standard_name`, `target_path`), so the "no unit" half of the justification is false, and the module docstring it corrects (`imas_ambix/data/eddb.py:25`, "no new engine and no cache-specific reader") already under-describes a raw reader that exists there (`read_eddb_token`, `imas_ambix/data/eddb.py:128`).

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §2's geometry script, §3's signals script and §3's `read_channel` each hide catalogue addressing, per-IDS reading and render orchestration behind a small interface; none spreads one piece of machinery across several shallow wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §2 duplicates the acquisition route owned by `imas_ambix/data/description_reader.py` and the per-IDS readers in `imas_ambix/gs/artifact_geometry.py`, both of which already read the same store.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — every section that touches a counted family accounts for it in its own text: §1b "adds nothing", §3 names `read_channel` as its one public addition and says it "retires nothing", §3's signals script "adds one script with no command-line option and no public name", and §4 names its one field and states it "retires nothing"; §2's script replaces the one §1b deletes, so the net public surface is zero.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §2 re-derives JT-60SA description-store addressing instead of citing `imas_ambix/data/description_reader.py`, whose docstring declares itself the sole machine-description acquisition route.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §3 adds `read_channel` as a second raw read path over the JT-60SA cache beside `ZarrTransformEngine`/`VirtualZarrView`, and its stated justification ("no time base and no unit") is contradicted by `VirtualArray.attrs`, which already exposes `units`.
